definitions.gloss: to clench one's teeth; to grit one's teeth
definitions.explanation: To press the upper and lower teeth tightly together. Used both literally (physical clenching) and figuratively to describe enduring pain, hardship, or frustration with determination.

examples.japanese: ⟦{歯|は}→歯：00778_ha⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{食|く}いしばって⟦{耐|た}えた→耐える：12087_taeru⟧。
examples.english: I gritted my teeth and endured it.

examples.japanese: ⟦{痛|いた}み→痛み：01795_itami⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{歯|は}→歯：00778_ha⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{食|く}いしばり⟦ながら→ながら：10530_nagara⟧、⟦ゴール→ゴール：03845_gooru⟧⟦まで→まで：00490_made⟧⟦{走|はし}り{続|つづ}けた→走り続ける：22070_hashiritsuzukeru⟧。
examples.english: Gritting my teeth against the pain, I kept running to the finish line.

examples.japanese: ⟦{悔|くや}しくて→悔しい：02343_kuyashii⟧⟦{涙|なみだ}→涙：02235_namida⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{出|で}→出る：00513_deru⟧そうだった⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧、⟦{歯|は}→歯：00778_ha⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{食|く}いしばって⟦{泣|な}かなかった→泣く：00655_naku⟧。
examples.english: I was so frustrated I nearly cried, but I gritted my teeth and held back the tears.

notes:
USAGE:
Almost always used in the phrase ⟦{歯|は}→歯：00778_ha⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{食|く}いしばる. The figurative meaning of enduring hardship with determination is very common and carries a strong emotional tone of perseverance.

Godan verb (る → ら/り/る/れ/ろ): {食|く}いしばらない, {食|く}いしばります, {食|く}いしばる, {食|く}いしばれば, {食|く}いしばろう

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ⟦{歯|は}→歯：00778_ha⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{食|く}いしばる (to clench/grit one's teeth)
- ⟦{歯|は}→歯：00778_ha⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{食|く}いしばって⟦{耐|た}える→耐える：12087_taeru⟧ (to grit one's teeth and endure)
- ⟦{歯|は}→歯：00778_ha⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{食|く}いしばって⟦{頑張|がんば}る→頑張る：01222_ganbaru⟧ (to grit one's teeth and persevere)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {食|く}いしばる: to clench teeth (endurance, determination)
- ⟦{噛|か}みしめる→噛みしめる：11997_kamishimeru⟧: to bite down on; to savor (can be physical or emotional)
- ⟦{我慢|がまん}する→我慢する：25343_gamansuru⟧: to endure, to put up with (broader, no physical image)
